hook: What if Britain’s highest peak conceals a 100-acre summit plateau?

sections.voiceover: What if Britain’s highest peak conceals a 100-acre summit plateau?
b_roll: Aerial view approaching the mountain summit plateau

sections.voiceover: In the Grampian Mountains near Fort William, Ben Nevis reaches 1,345 metres above sea level. How wide is this 1,345-metre Scottish Highlands giant?
b_roll: Topographical map showing Fort William and Grampian Mountains
Elevation comparison graphic between Ben Nevis and Snowdon

sections.voiceover: Yet, it claims a topographic isolation radius of 739 kilometres.
b_roll: Map radius circle expanding across 739 kilometres around Ben Nevis

sections.voiceover: The high plateau spans 100 acres with a steep northeast cliff. Those hikers climb past 4,413 feet of sheer elevation.
b_roll: Top-down view of the 100-acre summit plateau and northeast cliff face
Hikers ascending the trail in the Scottish Highlands

sections.voiceover: That 1,345-metre peak remains the highest point in the British Isles.
b_roll: Cinematic wide shot of the Ben Nevis peak towering over the landscape
